title: LessonPlanner: Assisting Novice Teachers to Prepare Pedagogy-Driven Lesson Plans with Large Language Models
venue: UIST ’24 (The 37th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge novice teachers face when preparing lesson plans: identifying effective pedagogical strategies, finding suitable materials, and organizing content into a coherent instructional flow. The authors argue that while large language models (LLMs) can generate useful teaching content, using them through a generic chat interface often produces fragmented, hard-to-manage outputs and requires substantial prompting skill and iterative refinement.

To address this, they develop LessonPlanner, a web-based interactive system powered by GPT-4 that structures lesson-plan creation around Bloom’s Taxonomy and Gagne’s Nine Events of Instruction. The system provides a goal-setting page, a block-based outline editor, preset prompts for common instructional activities, sidebar-based LLM assistance, and flexible editing/regeneration tools. The design was informed by a formative study with six novice teachers and teaching assistants.

The evaluation included a within-subjects study with 12 university students who acted as teachers and prepared lesson plans for familiar data-structures topics, plus expert interviews with six teachers from university, elementary, and high-school contexts. Compared with a baseline ChatGPT interface, LessonPlanner improved the rated quality of lesson plans and reduced workload. Interview findings also suggest that participants valued the pedagogy-driven structure and the more organized interaction model, but they raised concerns about the accuracy, subject-specific usefulness, and cognitive burden of prompting LLMs. The paper concludes with design implications for supporting teaching activities with LLMs.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: An OpenAI generative AI chatbot/LLM system used for conversational content generation and assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the baseline web app for lesson-plan preparation; also referenced by participants as an existing tool they had used to generate lesson-plan-related content such as answers to student questions.

findings.finding_summary: In the formative interviews, three participants reported prior use of ChatGPT for lesson preparation, but five participants expressed distrust of its outputs. Concerns included needing to double-check detailed content, inability to produce course-appropriate questions/materials, and a tendency for outputs to be useful only as a rough outline rather than directly usable lesson content.
findings.measure: Interview-reported perceptions of usefulness, accuracy, and subject-specific suitability of ChatGPT-generated lesson-plan content
findings.sample_size: n=6 (formative study); n=12 (within-subjects study participants had baseline access to ChatGPT)

quality_tier_rationale: The paper uses mixed methods: a formative interview/co-design study plus a within-subjects comparison, but the reported finding here is primarily qualitative and does not provide inferential effect estimates for ChatGPT itself. This supports a yellow tier rather than a higher-evidence tier.
impact_tier_rationale: The evidence for ChatGPT in this paper is mostly about user distrust and concerns rather than a measured positive or negative performance effect. Because no effect size is reported and the findings are mixed/qualitative, the impact is unclear.
